definition: to express disapproval or disappointment; blame
memoryTip: Re-PROACH: approach someone again—with blame, not praise.
correctPassage: There was quiet reproach in the way she asked why he had missed the deadline.
wrongPassages: After the championship win, the coach offered only reproach, listing each player's strengths in detail.
Her letter of reproach thanked him warmly for every favor he had done.
The board's formal reproach endorsed the policy and recommended a raise for the director.

memoryTip: Full of CONTEMPT—scornful, looking down on someone.
correctPassage: His contemptuous shrug made it clear he thought the proposal was foolish.
wrongPassages: She gave a contemptuous smile that radiated pure admiration for the speaker.
In a contemptuous show of respect, he stood and applauded the critic's argument.
The mentor's contemptuous comments on the draft were full of encouragement and praise.

memoryTip: Makes you START (jump)—so surprising you flinch.
correctPassage: The most startling finding was that sleep alone cut the error rate in half.
wrongPassages: Historians called the long-predicted election result startling, since polls had forecast it for months.
The lab reported a startling pattern: every trial matched the control with no unexpected deviation.
Her startling presentation simply repeated the three bullet points the team already knew by heart.

definition: to fail to give a true impression of; to contradict
memoryTip: Be-LIE: the surface lies about what is really underneath.
correctPassage: His calm tone belied how nervous he felt before the exam.
wrongPassages: Rising enrollment numbers belied the claim that the program was thriving.
Her tearful apology belied how sincerely sorry she felt after the mistake.
The detailed footnotes belied every source she cited, confirming each quotation line by line.

definition: peculiar to an individual; highly distinctive
memoryTip: IDIO + quirks: your personal odd habits and style.
correctPassage: Her idiosyncratic color code made the spreadsheet unreadable to anyone else on the team.
wrongPassages: Everyone followed the same idiosyncratic checklist issued by headquarters.
The style guide enforced one idiosyncratic format so that all reports looked identical.
Regulators praised the idiosyncratic protocol for eliminating personal variation across every lab.
